expectation.text: Research-grade multi-agent reasoning on a single machine with enforced epistemic discipline: independent analyses, adversarial verification, computational evidence through a dedicated executor, and material conclusions gated by a human, all driven through the Hermes Kanban board.

payload.observed: A maintained stack published at https://github.com/Lobachevski1998/hermes-stack runs six Hermes agent profiles as cooperating personas (director, science, genio, runner, audit, review), each a separate runtime home under ~/.hermes/profiles. The director plans the smallest sufficient workflow graph and never lets a worker completion imply validation; science and genio produce deliberately independent reasoning; runner carries numerical implementation; audit is adversarial over claims, numerics, provenance and epistemic status; review is the final integration gate. Two shell recipes wrap the board: a two-mode DAG (analysis without new computation; compute with a runner stage; either way science+genio then audit then review then director final) and a lighter swarm with two workers, an audit verifier and a review synthesizer. Persona files encode explicit category separation (observation, measurement, hypothesis, supported interpretation, validated numerical result, formal proof, inconclusive, refuted, superseded) and prohibit silent reconciliation of conflicting evidence. Event-driven dispatch uses a single post-create nudge plus the Gateway sweep as the recovery path, with concurrency treated as capacity rather than quota, and material conclusions reach the human through a public notification topic. The public repository ships sanitized persona and config examples only; memories, authentication state, sessions, logs and third-party skill packs are never redistributed (vendored skills are listed by name in a lockfile).
payload.title: Scientific six-persona multi-agent stack on Hermes: Kanban DAG and swarm orchestration with epistemic role separation
